title: Update SDK key format to {token}.{platform}_{geo}_{publicRandom}.{secret}_{sha1}
description:
The current SDK key format doesn't expose a clear public segment, which forces the proxy to compute and manage a separate hash for safe logging and telemetry. The new format introduces a structured three-part key where the first two dot-segments form a stable, non-sensitive public prefix that can be used directly — no derived identifier needed.

The new format:

```
{token}.{platform}_{geo}_{publicRandom}.{secret}_{sha1}
```

Example: `dt01.server_us_ab3xy9kp2q.03ee0ef7cd4244bfb8b71fea8f783f53_d4f8a9c12a`

This is a clean format update — no migration path required.

## Field specification

| Field | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | `dt[0-9]{2}` | e.g. `dt01` |
| `platform` | `web\|mobile\|server` | |
| `geo` | `[a-z]{2}` | e.g. `us`, `eu`, `ap`, `oc` |
| `publicRandom` | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{10}` | mixed case + digits for entropy |
| `secret` | `[a-f0-9]{32}` | UUIDv4 without hyphens |
| `sha1` | `[a-f0-9]{10,}` | first 10+ hex digits of SHA-1 over the full preceding key; length is open-ended |

## Public identifier and log safety

The public prefix is `{token}.{platform}_{geo}_{publicRandom}` (first two dot-segments). It is safe to include in logs, telemetry, support bundles, and structured metrics. The third dot-segment (`{secret}_{sha1}`) must never appear in any logged output.

**Canonical redaction rule (language-agnostic):** split on `.`, drop the last segment, rejoin on `.`.

**Validate or match a public-only slug** (identity + public segment; no private segment):
```
^(dt[0-9]{2})\.(web|mobile|server)_([a-z]{2})_([a-zA-Z0-9]{10})$
```
Capture groups: `version`, `platform`, `geo`, `publicRandom`.

**Strip the private segment from a full key for safe logging** — group 1 is the log-safe prefix; group 2 is the private segment and must not be written to logs. The `sha1` length is open-ended (`{10,}`) to allow future growth without re-issuing keys:
```
^(dt[0-9]{2}\.(?:web|mobile|server)_[a-z]{2}_[a-zA-Z0-9]{10})\.([a-f0-9]{32}_[a-f0-9]{10,})$
```

## Context

Because the public prefix is now structurally unambiguous, the proxy no longer needs to derive or store a separate hash for logging. Any place that currently computes a key fingerprint for telemetry or log correlation can be replaced with a simple split-and-drop operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- SDK key validation regex updated throughout the proxy to match the new three-part format
- Log-safe redaction helper implemented using the canonical split-on-dot rule; existing fingerprint/hash derivation removed
- All internal logs, telemetry labels, and structured metrics use the public prefix (`{token}.{platform}_{geo}_{publicRandom}`) as the key identifier — never the full key
- OTel spans that include a path containing the SDK key must record the public prefix and a redaction notice (e.g. `<redacted>`) in place of the private segment, in line with OTel semantic conventions for sensitive attributes
- Full-key validation (including `secret` length and `sha1` verification) implemented per the spec above
- Existing tests updated; new tests cover: valid full key, valid public-only slug, full-key redaction, reject malformed keys
- No changes to how keys are stored or transmitted — format change only affects parsing and validation

title: Replace UPSTREAM_CDN_URL with geo-bound CDN routing derived from SDK key
description:
The proxy currently routes all upstream CDN requests to a single UPSTREAM_CDN_URL, which breaks data sovereignty requirements. Dynatrace uses geo-bound CDN domains (e.g. cdn.us.fm.dynatracelabs.com, cdn.eu.fm.dynatracelabs.com) per region, and the region is encoded in the SDK key itself (format: dt_server_{region}_{token}).

Replace UPSTREAM_CDN_URL with CDN_BASE_DOMAIN (e.g. fm.dynatracelabs.com). On each request, extract the region from the SDK key and derive the full upstream URL as: https://cdn.{region}.{CDN_BASE_DOMAIN}/server/{sdkKey}.json

Changes required:
- internal/config/config.go: remove UpstreamCDNURL, add CDNBaseDomain (env CDN_BASE_DOMAIN, required, validated as non-empty hostname)
- internal/proxy/handler.go: replace upstream *url.URL field with cdnBaseDomain string; rewrite buildTarget to derive geo-bound URL from SDK key; add extractRegion(sdkKey) helper (splits on _ with SplitN limit 4, validates dt_server_{region}_{token} format); update ServeHTTP to call buildTarget before cache lookup and return 400 for unrecognized key format; update serveMiss signature to accept pre-built upstreamURL
- cmd/proxy/main.go: pass cfg.CDNBaseDomain to proxy.New()
- internal/proxy/handler_test.go: update constructor calls and expected upstream URLs; add extractRegion unit tests

cache.Entry.FetchURL stores the derived geo-bound URL, so background refresh (Fetch) requires no changes.
close_reason: Implemented: extractRegion + buildTarget derive geo-bound URL from SDK key. CDN_BASE_DOMAIN replaces UPSTREAM_CDN_URL. Region validated [a-z0-9-] (SSRF guard). 23 tests passing.

title: Integration test harness
description: The proxy acceptance criteria require end-to-end verification that unit tests cannot cover (cache behavior under simulated outages, SSE fan-out invariants, billing flush under SIGTERM). Build an in-process test harness with: a mock upstream CDN server, a mock SSE server emitting refetchEvaluation events and lifecycle events, and a mock billing endpoint. Use the harness to test all acceptance criteria from the technical spec: cache hit/miss, outage behavior (503 for uncached, 200 for cached), startup sequence cases, SSE fan-out (N clients = 1 upstream connection), billing accuracy, shutdown flush.
close_reason: Integration test harness implemented with CDN/SSE/billing mocks, 31 tests passing. Also fixed nil guard on snapshot.Writer.enqueue.

title: Lifecycle event handlers (token rotation, stage/project deletion)
description: Rotated or invalidated SDK keys must stop serving cached config. All lifecycle SSE events (token rotation, release stage deletion, project deletion) are handled the same way: the upstream event must carry the affected SDK key(s). For each affected key: compute SHA-256(key), drop the cache entry, delete the persisted snapshot, close fan-out connections. The 5-minute TTL fallback covers any missed SSE events — worst-case staleness window is 5 minutes, which must be documented in operator-facing materials.

title: Rewrite SSE URL in proxied flagd config JSON
description: The flagd config JSON served by Cloudflare CDN contains an embedded SSE URL pointing to the upstream SSE service (Ably/ingest abstraction). If the proxy returns this URL verbatim, SDKs would connect directly to the upstream for SSE, bypassing the proxy's fan-out and violating the in-network constraint. When serving cached config to SDKs, rewrite the SSE URL to point to the proxy's own SSE endpoint (derived from the proxy's configured base URL + the SSE path). SDKs must use the proxy for both config fetches and SSE subscriptions.

title: SSE fan-out endpoint for SDKs
description: SDKs must receive real-time flag change notifications from the proxy. Expose GET /sse as the proxy's SSE endpoint. Authentication uses the SDK key via the same mechanism as config fetches. Fan-out group is keyed by SHA-256(sdk_key). Re-broadcast upstream refetchEvaluation events verbatim to all connected clients for that key. SDKs configured with proxyUrl use proxyUrl+/sse for SSE — the SSE URL in the flagd config JSON is ignored when proxied. Event format: event: message, data: {type: refetchEvaluation, etag, lastModified} per OFREP ADR-0008.
close_reason: Implemented GET /sse fan-out endpoint with sdk_key query param auth, cache-gate (412), per-client SSE streaming, heartbeat keepalive, SSEClientConnections and SSEEventsDelivered metrics. 9 tests passing.

title: Upstream SSE client (one connection per flag set)
description: N SDK client instances using the same SDK key must produce exactly one upstream SSE connection. The upstream SSE URL is read from the cached flagd config payload — no upstream SSE connection is opened until the config for that key has been cached. Subscribe as a generic SSE client (OFREP ADR-0008 format: refetchEvaluation events). Reconnect with exponential backoff. Only establish/re-establish upstream SSE connections when upstream is reachable; if upstream is unreachable at startup (serving from snapshot), do not attempt SSE until a fresh config can be fetched.
close_reason: Implemented upstream SSE client with one connection per SDK key; all quality gates pass

title: Shutdown flush on SIGTERM
description: When the proxy is scaled down or redeployed, usage counts from the final interval must not be silently lost. On SIGTERM: immediately stop accepting new SDK connections, drain in-flight request counters, attempt one final billing flush. Wait for the flush to succeed or a 10-second grace period to expire (whichever comes first). Log any counts that could not be flushed before exiting. Exit cleanly with code 0.

title: Telemetry retry buffer with bounded overflow
description: Transient billing endpoint outages must not cause silent data loss. Implement a bounded in-memory buffer for failed flush batches. On the next flush cycle, retry buffered batches before the new batch. When the buffer is full, drop the oldest entry, log the drop event, and increment an OTel metric so operators are aware of usage data loss. Configurable buffer size.

title: Batch-and-flush telemetry reporter
description: Usage counts must be reported to the billing endpoint on a regular cadence without blocking SDK request handling. Implement a batch-and-flush reporter that drains per-token counters on a configurable interval (default 60s, min 10s) and sends the batch to the BillingReporter interface. Each batch includes: per-token request counts, time-window start/end timestamps, and proxy instance identity. Authenticate each flush with the SDK token. On endpoint unreachability, pass the batch to the retry buffer.

title: Per-SDK-token request counter
description: Dynatrace bills based on actual SDK usage, not upstream request volume. Cache hits must count. Implement a thread-safe per-SDK-token counter that increments on every incoming SDK HTTP request, regardless of whether it was served from cache or from upstream. Counter is the data source for the telemetry reporter.

title: Define and mock billing endpoint interface
description: M3 telemetry work must not be blocked on the real billing endpoint contract being finalized. Define an internal Go interface (BillingReporter) that encapsulates the billing flush contract. Implement an in-process mock that satisfies the interface and records calls for testing. Document the expected real contract (payload schema, auth, back-pressure) as the interface spec so the real implementation is a drop-in replacement.

title: Startup sequence (4-case logic)
description: The proxy must never silently start with no data source. Implement the startup sequence: (1) upstream reachable — start normally, load snapshots if persistence configured; (2) upstream unreachable + persistence configured + snapshot fresh — load snapshot, serve, retry upstream in background; (3) upstream unreachable + persistence configured + stale snapshot — load snapshot, loud warning + metric, retry; (4) upstream unreachable + persistence not configured or no snapshot — exit non-zero so Kubernetes restarts and surfaces the failure. Wire into the /ready probe.

title: S3-compatible snapshot persistence
description: A proxy restart during an upstream outage must not reset the cache to empty. Implement an S3-compatible persistence backend that writes a snapshot asynchronously after each cache update. Persistence is optional — if not configured, this backend is not initialized and snapshots are skipped entirely. The snapshot envelope: snapshot_version, sdk_key_hash, etag (from upstream CDN ETag header), captured_at, payload (opaque bytes). Snapshots are keyed by sdk_key_hash. Snapshot writes are never on the hot path — a failed write logs a warning and increments an OTel metric but does not fail the SDK request. A 304 on TTL re-fetch does not trigger a snapshot write (nothing changed). Read snapshots on startup to restore cache state.

title: In-memory cache with 5-minute TTL
description: Without a cache, every SDK request causes an upstream CDN round trip, defeating the proxy's purpose. Implement a thread-safe in-memory cache keyed by SHA-256(sdk_key) (truncated to 16 hex chars). Each entry holds the flagd config payload and the ETag from the upstream CDN response. Entries are populated lazily on first request. On 5-minute TTL expiry, re-fetch using If-None-Match with the stored ETag: a 304 resets the TTL with no snapshot write or fan-out; a 200 updates the entry, writes the snapshot, and fans out. SSE events refresh the cache immediately. The proxy treats the payload as opaque bytes.
close_reason: Implemented cache.Cache, cache.Refresher, and integrated into proxy.Handler. Tests cover hit/miss/304/503 paths, TTL staleness, concurrent access, and refresher behavior.

title: OCI container image and CI pipeline
description: The proxy must ship as a single self-contained container image with no sidecars. Build a multi-stage Dockerfile (Go builder stage + distroless runtime stage) that produces a minimal, statically-linked binary. Wire GitHub Actions CI to run build, test, and lint on every push, and push a tagged image to the container registry on release tags.

Before implementing snapshot writes, the team must decide: the version field name (snapshot_version), integer vs semver, and forward-compatibility policy (how older proxy versions read newer snapshots and vice versa). This is a design decision that must be made before the snapshot persistence implementation is built. Schedule a sync with Engineering to resolve.

title: OpenTelemetry metrics foundation

Wire the OTel Go SDK with an OTLP exporter and define all metric instruments up front per the alerting plan: request volume by status (cache hit/miss/upstream error/client error), upstream SSE connection state per flag set, cache size per flag set, snapshot age per flag set, billing flush success/failure counts, billing buffer size, billing flush lag, startup path taken, snapshot write success/failure counts.

title: Kubernetes health probes (/health, /ready, /live)

These endpoints are required for any Kubernetes deployment to function correctly.

title: Flagd config passthrough with token passthrough auth
description: Server-side SDKs must be able to route flagd config JSON fetches through the proxy instead of directly to Cloudflare CDN. Proxy incoming GET requests to the upstream CDN URL, forwarding the SDK token from the incoming request as the auth credential. The proxy holds no credentials of its own. Return the upstream response verbatim (for now; SSE URL rewriting is a separate M4 issue).

title: HTTP server skeleton with graceful shutdown

Implement the server using stdlib mux (or chi), wire SIGTERM/SIGINT handling with a configurable drain timeout, and load configuration from environment variables (port, upstream CDN URL, log level). This is the skeleton all M1 handlers plug into.

Set up: Go module (go.mod), /cmd/proxy entrypoint, /internal package layout, Makefile with build/test/lint targets, Dockerfile skeleton (multi-stage with distroless), .gitignore, and a GitHub Actions CI stub (build + test on push). This is a prerequisite for all implementation work.

title: SSE: reuse channel query param as stream_id instead of deriving a separate identifier
description:
SSE connections always include a `channel` query parameter — a SHA-1 40-character hex of the SDK key. The proxy currently derives its own `stream_id` for internal correlation, which is redundant: the `channel` value is already a stable, key-scoped identifier computed upstream.

Reusing `channel` as the `stream_id` eliminates a derivation step and aligns the proxy's internal SSE identity with the value already present on the wire.

## Context

Related to sdk-proxy-78x, which introduces a structured SDK key format with a clear public prefix. The `channel` parameter predates that work and is already in use as a per-connection identifier — it just isn't being leveraged internally.

## Acceptance criteria

- `stream_id` replaced by `channel` value throughout SSE connection handling
- No new hash or ID derivation for SSE stream correlation
- Existing SSE tests updated to reflect the simplified identifier
- `channel` value validated as 40-character lowercase hex on connection open; malformed values rejected with an appropriate error response
close_reason: Won't implement: the premise that 'channel is already on the wire' is incorrect. The proxy's client-facing SSE endpoint uses stream_id=PublicID(sdk_key) — not a channel param. The upstream SSE URL does use channels=SHA1(full_sdk_key), but the proxy already hides that URL from providers via rewrite. Providers never construct the channel value independently; they follow whatever URL is embedded in the config. Implementing this revision would add a SHA-1 computation, a secondary sha1→publicID reverse map in cache, and eviction cleanup in all three eviction paths — real complexity for a benefit that isn't exercised in normal flow. Current stream_id=PublicID design is correct: it's the cache key, standardized in sdk-proxy-78x, and appropriately opaque.

title: Validate and define SSE endpoint behavior when SDK key config has not yet been cached
description:
The proxy design invariant ensures upstream SSE connections are never opened before config is cached for a given SDK key. However, there is no validated behavior for the client-facing GET /sse endpoint when a fresh proxy receives an SSE connection request before any config has been fetched for that key.

The expected outcome is a connection rejection, but the HTTP response code, headers, and — critically — the downstream OpenFeature provider's recovery path have not been tested or explicitly defined. A provider that enters an unrecoverable error state on cold-start rejection would require manual intervention to restore healthy flag evaluation.
design:
Related design invariants from CLAUDE.md:
- 'SSE after config: upstream SSE connections are only opened after the config for that SDK key is cached. Never open an upstream SSE connection for a key whose config has never been fetched.'
- '503 on uncached miss during outage: do not return an empty config. An empty response is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty flag set.'

The 503 + Retry-After pattern from the second invariant likely applies here too. A 401 would be misleading — the key may be valid, the proxy simply has not seen it yet.
acceptance_criteria:
- HTTP response returned by GET /sse when no config is cached is explicitly defined (503 + Retry-After is the likely correct choice — this is a readiness failure, not an auth failure)
- OpenFeature provider does not enter an unrecoverable state on SSE rejection at cold start
- Provider auto-recovers to READY state once the proxy bootstraps (config cached via a flag evaluation request)
- Retry and backoff behavior expected from the provider is documented
- Integration test covers the sequence: fresh proxy → SSE connect → rejection → flag eval → proxy bootstraps → SSE reconnect → provider READY

title: Emit structured startup log of resolved configuration with secrets redacted
description:
The proxy currently starts without logging its resolved configuration. Operators have no way to confirm — without attaching a debugger or reading source — which effective values are in use, whether a custom override was picked up, or which optional features are active. This is especially painful when diagnosing misconfiguration in Kubernetes where env vars come from multiple sources (ConfigMaps, Secrets, Downward API).

A single structured log line at startup, emitted after config is loaded and validated, solves this.

## Changes required

### internal/config/config.go — add LogValue()
Add a `LogValue() slog.Value` method on `Config` that returns a `slog.GroupValue` with one attribute per field. Fields typed as `Secret` already implement `slog.LogValuer` and will emit `[REDACTED]` automatically — no extra handling needed.

Fields to include and their log key names:
- port → `port`
- CDNBaseDomain → `cdn_base_domain`
- LogLevel → `log_level`
- ShutdownTimeout → `shutdown_timeout`
- OTLPEnabled → `otlp_enabled`
- BillingFlushInterval → `billing_flush_interval`
- BillingRetryBufferSize → `billing_retry_buffer_size`
- ProxyInstanceID → `proxy_instance_id`
- LifecycleKeysCap → `lifecycle_keys_cap`
- SSEDisabled → `sse_disabled`
- SnapshotBackend → `snapshot_backend` (empty string → log as "disabled")
- SnapshotS3Bucket → `snapshot_s3_bucket`
- SnapshotS3Region → `snapshot_s3_region`
- SnapshotS3Endpoint → `snapshot_s3_endpoint`
- SnapshotS3Prefix → `snapshot_s3_prefix`
- SnapshotS3AccessKey → `snapshot_s3_access_key` (Secret → [REDACTED])
- SnapshotS3SecretKey → `snapshot_s3_secret_key` (Secret → [REDACTED])
- SnapshotLocalDir → `snapshot_local_dir`
- SnapshotWriteQueueSize → `snapshot_write_queue_size`
- SnapshotMaxAge → `snapshot_max_age`
- CacheInactivityEvictAfter → `cache_inactivity_evict_after`

### cmd/proxy/main.go — emit the log
After `config.FromEnv()` succeeds (around line 42), add:
```go
slog.Info("starting sdk-proxy", "config", cfg)
```
This leverages `cfg.LogValue()` automatically via slog's LogValuer interface.

### internal/config/config_test.go / secret_test.go
- Add a test that logs a `Config` with secrets set and asserts the output contains `[REDACTED]` and does not contain the raw secret value
- Verify that a `Config` with all zero values produces a valid log (no panic)

## Acceptance criteria
- Proxy emits a single `INFO` log line at startup with all resolved config values
- `SNAPSHOT_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `SNAPSHOT_S3_SECRET_KEY` appear as `[REDACTED]` in the log
- No other env-var value that could be a credential leaks as plaintext
- The log is emitted after validation — it always reflects the final effective config
- Unit test asserts secret redaction
- make lint passes
notes: The Secret type (internal/config/secret.go) already implements slog.LogValuer returning [REDACTED]. No new redaction logic needed — the LogValue() method on Config just needs to include those fields and slog handles the rest. Do not use fmt.Sprintf or json.Marshal to build the log message — always go through slog so the LogValuer chain fires correctly.

### Docs

title: feat(cache): lazy revalidation of snapshot-loaded entries on first request
description:
When the proxy loads flag set configuration from a snapshot at startup, the loaded entries may be up to SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE old (default 24h). Today the background refresher eventually revalidates them, but the timing depends on the SSE-driven poll interval (up to 10 min). This means a snapshot-loaded entry can be served stale for minutes after the first SDK request arrives.

The fix: on the first cache hit for a snapshot-loaded entry whose FetchedAt is older than the current refresh interval, trigger an immediate background conditional GET (If-None-Match). This is demand-driven — entries no one requests never generate CDN traffic. A 304 resets FetchedAt; a 200 replaces the cache entry and triggers an async snapshot write.

This replaces the 'eager revalidation of all entries at startup' approach from sdk-proxy-dsl, which was closed because it would unconditionally poll CDN for every snapshot-loaded key even if most are never used.

## Acceptance criteria
- On a cache hit for a snapshot-loaded entry where time.Since(entry.FetchedAt) > currentRefreshInterval, a background conditional GET is fired before the response is served (response is not delayed)
- The background conditional GET uses the existing cache.Fetcher interface
- A 304 resets FetchedAt only (no snapshot write)
- A 200 updates payload + ETag + FetchedAt and triggers async snapshot write
- An entry is only revalidated once per refresh interval (guard against double-fire on concurrent requests)
- No parsing of the flagd config payload
- Metric proxy.snapshot.demand_revalidation.total emitted with result=hit|refreshed|error
notes: Revised approach: synchronous conditional GET on first stale hit. The original AC said 'response is not delayed' — this has been revised after discussion: we prioritize accuracy (fresh config on first hit) over latency (one CDN round-trip delay for the first stale snapshot-loaded request). Subsequent requests within the refresh interval are served immediately from cache. On CDN error/429/5xx: fall back to cached payload (never block an SDK response). On 4xx (401/403/404/410): evict entry, write 503 to client (next request is a cold miss that will pass through the real 4xx). Metric labels expanded from hit|refreshed|error to: hit (not stale, no CDN call), not_modified (304), refreshed (200), evicted (4xx), preserved_stale (429/5xx), error (network). Note: demand-reval singleflight is independent of the bg tick singleflight — a narrow window exists where both may issue a CDN request for the same key concurrently; this is benign (no correctness issue).

title: feat(snapshot): runtime cross-proxy snapshot fallback on CDN failure
description:
During a CDN outage, proxies in a cluster that missed a config update before the outage began will serve stale flag sets for the entire outage duration. Proxies share an S3-compatible snapshot backend, so a proxy that did fetch the latest config before the outage will have written a newer snapshot. Today, running proxies never re-read from the snapshot store — it is read-at-startup-only. This means the newer snapshot written by one proxy is invisible to its peers until they restart.

The fix: when a background CDN refresh fails (5xx or network error), the proxy should asynchronously check the shared snapshot store for a newer entry. If the snapshot's captured_at is more recent than the current in-memory FetchedAt AND the etag differs, load the snapshot payload into the in-memory cache. This must not block the response path and must not parse the flag set payload (ETags remain the sole freshness signal).

Known limitation: this only helps when at least one proxy in the cluster successfully fetched and persisted a newer snapshot before Cloudflare became unreachable. If all proxies lost CDN access simultaneously before any wrote an updated snapshot, S3 has nothing newer to offer. This is expected and acceptable.
design:
A new ADR is required before implementation. The ADR must cover:
- The decision to use the snapshot store as a passive cross-proxy propagation channel during CDN outages (read path extended from startup-only to on-failure)
- Debounce strategy: during a CDN outage the background poller fires every 10s per key; without debouncing, each tick triggers an S3 Get. The ADR must align on the debounce interval (candidate: once per refresh interval per key, ~1 min) and where that state lives
- Update condition: captured_at > FetchedAt AND etag != currentETag (conservative — no update if payload unchanged)
- Whether a successful snapshot load should reset FetchedAt and trigger a snapshot write (likely yes for FetchedAt, no for snapshot write since the proxy did not independently verify with CDN)
- Async vs inline: S3 Get must be async (goroutine) so CDN failure path remains fast
acceptance_criteria:
- A new ADR (docs/adr/) documents the cross-proxy fallback design and debounce strategy before any code is merged
- On a failed CDN refresh for key K, the proxy initiates an async S3 Get for K's snapshot
- The async check is debounced per key — the interval and mechanism must match whatever the ADR aligns on
- Update condition: snapshot captured_at > current FetchedAt AND snapshot etag != current ETag; no-op otherwise
- The response path (handler returning 503 or cached payload) is not blocked by the S3 check
- The flag set payload is never parsed; ETags are the sole freshness comparator
- A successful snapshot load emits a metric (name TBD in ADR) with enough labels to distinguish outage-driven loads from startup loads
- If the S3 read itself fails, behavior is identical to today: serve in-memory payload, log warning, increment existing error metric
- snapshot persistence must be configured (SNAPSHOT_BACKEND set) for this path to activate; proxies without persistence are unaffected
- Unit and integration tests cover: newer snapshot loaded, same-etag no-op, S3 failure no-op, debounce suppresses redundant checks

title: feat(snapshot): eager background revalidation for snapshot-loaded entries on startup
description:
On CaseSnapshotFresh and CaseSnapshotStale startup paths, the background refresher uses the snapshot's captured_at as FetchedAt. Because the connected-SSE poll interval is 10 minutes, a snapshot that is just under SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE (default 24h) could be served for up to 10 additional minutes before the first ETag revalidation. This is the real freshness gap — not metadata.version (which would require breaking the payload-opaque invariant).

The fix: after LoadAll completes, trigger an immediate background conditional GET (If-None-Match) for every snapshot-loaded cache entry, without blocking /ready. A 304 resets FetchedAt; a 200 replaces the cache entry and triggers a snapshot write. Pure ETag-based, no payload parsing.
acceptance_criteria:
- When startup path is snapshot or snapshot_stale, all loaded entries receive an immediate background conditional GET before the first refresher tick
- /ready is not blocked by these re-fetches
- A 304 response resets FetchedAt only (no snapshot write, consistent with existing refresher behavior)
- A 200 response updates payload + ETag + FetchedAt and triggers async snapshot write
- No parsing of the flagd config payload — ETags remain the sole freshness signal
- Metric proxy.snapshot.startup_revalidation.total emitted with result=hit (304) or result=refreshed (200) or result=error
close_reason: Acceptance criteria (eager revalidation of all snapshot-loaded entries at startup) superseded by a demand-driven design. Two new issues capture the revised intent: lazy on-demand revalidation on first request, and inactivity-based cache eviction to stop polling unused keys.

description:
The proxy currently emits OTel metrics but has no distributed tracing. Adding traces will give Dynatrace visibility into per-request latency, upstream CDN calls, SSE connection lifecycle, and cache hit/miss paths.

title: Dynamic cache TTL based on SSE connection state
description:
## Why

The proxy currently uses a static cache TTL regardless of whether a live SSE connection exists for a given SDK key. This diverges from documented flagd provider behavior: when SSE is connected, change notifications make aggressive polling redundant and wasteful; when SSE is disconnected or disabled, polling is the only update mechanism and must be frequent.

## What needs to be done

Update the cache TTL refresh loop so that the effective poll interval for each SDK key is determined by its current SSE connection state:

| SSE state | Poll interval | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Connected | 10m | SSE notifies of changes; polling is a safety net |
| Disconnected / reconnecting | 10s | May be missing notifications; poll aggressively |
| Disabled (by config) | 10s | Polling is the only update mechanism |

**Constraints:**
- Intervals are fixed — not user-configurable. Only disabling SSE is configurable.
- Each CDN request has a hardcoded 5s timeout (intentionally less than the 10s minimum poll interval to prevent overlapping requests).
- TTL logic must consult SSE state per SDK key (keyed by `SHA-256(sdk_key)` — same key used by cache and SSE fan-out components).

## Acceptance criteria

- Cache refresh interval for a key drops to 10s when its SSE connection is lost or is in a reconnecting state.
- Cache refresh interval for a key returns to 10m once SSE reconnects successfully.
- When SSE is disabled globally by config, all keys use 10s.
- No interval values are exposed as user-configurable settings.
- CDN fetch timeout remains 5s.
- Existing unit and integration tests pass; new tests cover the three SSE states.

title: Improve empty_persistence startup: allow cold start when store is empty but reachable
description:
When persistence is configured but the snapshot store is empty, the proxy currently exits with code 1 unconditionally. This breaks two legitimate real-world scenarios:

1. First-ever deployment with persistence configured from day one — the store is empty by definition, but upstream CDN is reachable.
2. Disaster recovery — the snapshot store was wiped, but upstream is reachable and the proxy could recover on its own.

In both cases the proxy could start cold, warm its cache from upstream, and begin writing snapshots normally. Instead it hard-exits, requiring operators to either (a) do a two-step deploy (cold first, then enable persistence) or (b) manually pre-populate the store.

The fix should distinguish between:
- Store reachable but empty → start cold with a loud warning (same behavior as CaseColdNoPersistence but with an added metric/log)
- Store unreachable → retain the current fatal exit (misconfiguration or infra failure)

A SNAPSHOT_ALLOW_COLD_START=true escape hatch is one option; another is making the cold-on-empty path the default and only exiting when the store itself is unreachable.

Acceptance criteria:
- A first-time deploy with SNAPSHOT_BACKEND configured and an empty store starts successfully
- The startup path metric records a distinct value (e.g. empty_persistence_cold) so operators can see this happened
- Store-unreachable at startup still exits non-zero
- The snapshot.md docs are updated to reflect the new behavior

title: Cap sdkKeys/sdkKeyHashes array size in lifecycle event parser
description: The lifecycle event parseKeyHashes function accepts unbounded sdkKeyHashes and sdkKeys arrays from upstream SSE events. A malformed or compromised upstream could send thousands of entries, triggering one SHA-256 hash per sdkKeys entry on the SSE receive goroutine (CPU-amplification DoS vector). Add a combined cap (e.g. refuse events with more than 1000 total entries) in parseKeyHashes and return false with a warning log when exceeded.

title: Update docs/sse.md to document current and planned SSE behavior
description:
docs/sse.md exists but will be stale after sdk-proxy-qi8 and sdk-proxy-jj5 land, and it currently under-documents the two-leg connection model.

Updates needed:
1. Client endpoint section: replace sdk_key query param with stream_id; explain that stream_id is the SHA-256 hash of the SDK key (first 16 hex chars), not the key itself, and why (raw keys must not appear in URLs/logs).
2. Prerequisite message: replace /v1/config/{sdk_key}.json reference with /server/{sdk_key}.json.
3. Add a 'Two-Leg Connection Model' section that clearly explains:
   - Leg 1 (Provider → Proxy): client connects to GET /sse?stream_id=<hash>; stream_id is sourced from the rewritten SSE URL embedded in the flagd config returned by /server/{sdk_key}.json.
   - Leg 2 (Proxy → Upstream): proxy opens exactly one connection per SDK key to the original SSE URL from the flagd config (scheme, path, and query params preserved verbatim); no auth headers added.
   - How the stream_id in the client URL maps to the correct upstream connection internally.
4. No auth header is required or accepted on the client endpoint — the stream_id in the query string is the only identifier needed.

title: SSE URL rewrite: use stream_id (SDK key hash) instead of raw sdk_key
description:
The proxy currently rewrites the upstream SSE URL in the flagd config to <proxy>/sse?sdk_key=<raw_sdk_key>. This exposes the raw SDK key in URLs (which appear in access logs, reverse proxy logs, browser history), violating the project invariant: raw SDK keys must never appear in persistent identifiers.

Change proxySSEURL() in internal/proxy/handler.go to inject a stream_id parameter containing the SDK key hash instead:
  <proxy>/sse?stream_id=<16-char-hex-hash>

This keeps the SSE subsystem routing logic identical (manager is already keyed by sdkKeyHash), just removes the raw key from the URL and uses a name that accurately reflects the value (a stream identifier, not a credential).

Changes required:
1. internal/proxy/handler.go — proxySSEURL() accepts sdkKeyHash instead of raw sdkKey; injects ?stream_id=<hash>; call site passes cache.Key(sdkKey).
2. internal/sse/handler.go — extract stream_id query param instead of sdk_key; value is already a hash so skip validateSDKKeyRegion() and cache.Key() call; add simple hex-string validation.

The proxy → upstream SSE connection (conn.sseURL = original URL from flagd config) is unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented: SSE handler now reads stream_id (SDK key hash) instead of raw sdk_key. IncrementByHash added for billing path. All quality gates passed.

title: Register proxy handler at /server/ instead of catch-all /

Add a 404 fallback for / so unknown paths return a proper error. extractSDKKey already takes the final path segment, so no handler logic changes. Update any test fixtures using different path prefixes.

title: Improve background cache refresh log messages

The messages are ambiguous to anyone reading logs without deep knowledge of the code.\n\nUpdate both messages in internal/cache/cache.go to be self-explanatory: describe the upstream response (304 = content unchanged, 200 = new content), the action taken (TTL extended vs cache updated), and the context (background refresh).

title: Redact SnapshotS3SecretKey in Config to prevent credential leakage
description:
The SnapshotS3SecretKey field on internal/config/config.go Config struct is a plain string. If Config is ever serialized wholesale to logs or a debug endpoint (e.g. with %+v or json.Marshal), the AWS secret access key would leak in plaintext.

**What needs to be done:**
Wrap the secret in a redacting type, e.g.:
  type Secret string
  func (s Secret) String() string { return "[REDACTED]" }
  func (s Secret) LogValue() slog.Value { return slog.StringValue("[REDACTED]") }

Or, audit all log/diagnostic call sites to confirm Config is never logged whole — and add a linter rule or test to keep it that way.

Also ensure SnapshotS3AccessKey follows the same treatment if warranted.

**Why this matters:** AWS credentials in logs are a common source of secret sprawl. Low risk today (no debug endpoint exists), but worth closing before one is added.

description: The proxy handles three lifecycle events via SSE: SDK token rotation, release stage deletion, and project deletion. Before M4 lifecycle work begins, we need to confirm with the flag management service team which of these events are already emitted by the upstream system, and what their event type values are in the JSON data payload (per OFREP ADR-0008 format). Non-blocking: the proxy ships with the 5-minute TTL as a fallback for any events not yet available.

title: Rename health probe endpoints to Kubernetes-standard /livez, /readyz, /healthz
description:
The proxy currently exposes /live, /ready, and /health. The Kubernetes API convention (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/health-checks/) uses the /livez and /readyz suffixed form. /healthz exists but is deprecated in Kubernetes since v1.16 in favor of the split livez/readyz pattern.

Aligning to this convention makes the proxy a better drop-in for Kubernetes-native tooling and avoids operator confusion when they follow standard Kubernetes health check documentation.

## Changes required

### Code
- **cmd/proxy/main.go** (lines 227–229): rename route registrations to /livez, /readyz, /healthz
- **test/e2e/harness.go** (lines 205–206): update route registrations to match
- **internal/health/health_test.go**: update all request paths (/live → /livez, /ready → /readyz, /health → /healthz)

### Backward compatibility
Register the old paths (/live, /ready, /health) as aliases that redirect (301) or forward to the new paths, so existing Kubernetes manifests do not break silently on upgrade. Document the aliases as deprecated in the endpoint table and note a future version will remove them.

### Docs — update all occurrences of old paths
- **README.md**: Endpoints table (lines 129–131), Kubernetes YAML example (lines 66, 70)
- **docs/configuration.md**: Kubernetes YAML example (lines 416, 422)
- **docs/monitoring.md**: health probe table (lines 109–111), Kubernetes YAML (lines 120, 127), prose references (lines 95, 113, 134)
- **docs/operations.md** (new doc, sdk-proxy-cga): include /livez, /readyz, /healthz from the start — do not write /live, /ready, /health
- Any ADR that documents health probe design

## Acceptance criteria
- /livez returns 200 always; /readyz and /healthz return 200 only after snapshot load (or immediately if no persistence)
- /live, /ready, /health return 301 to their /z equivalents (backward compat)
- All docs updated — no remaining references to the old paths except in the deprecation notice
- All unit and e2e tests updated and passing
- make lint passes
notes: Kubernetes deprecated /healthz (the catch-all) in v1.16. The recommended pattern is to expose /livez (is the process alive?) and /readyz (is it ready to serve traffic?) as separate endpoints. The proxy's /health has always been an alias for /ready, so /healthz → /readyz alias is the right mapping. The 301 backward-compat aliases are important because Kubernetes manifests in the wild (including our own README and docs/configuration.md examples) reference the old paths.

title: Create docs/operations.md: operator-focused guide covering runtime behavior and failure conditions
description:
Operators deploying sdk-proxy need a single document that explains how the proxy behaves end-to-end — not just what knobs to turn, but what the proxy is actually doing at runtime and what happens when things go wrong. That understanding is currently scattered across cache.md, sse.md, snapshot.md, monitoring.md, and shutdown.md with no narrative thread connecting them.

## What to create

**docs/operations.md** — a prose-first operator guide. Target reader: someone responsible for running sdk-proxy in production who needs a mental model, not just a config table.

## Sections to cover

**Normal operation**
- Full request lifecycle: SDK client → proxy (cache hit path vs. cold miss → CDN fetch → cache fill) → response
- SSE fan-out lifecycle: how the proxy opens exactly one upstream SSE connection per SDK key, when it opens (after first config fetch), and how it rebroadcasts refetchEvaluation to N downstream clients
- Dynamic poll interval: 10 min while SSE is connected, 10 s when disconnected/reconnecting — and why the difference matters operationally
- Cache key scheme: SHA-256(sdk_key) truncated to 16 hex chars — implications for storage, logs, and metrics
- ETag revalidation: what a 304 does vs. what a 200 does (TTL reset only vs. cache fill + snapshot write + SSE fan-out)

**Failure conditions** (draw from test/e2e/outage_test.go, startup_test.go, lifecycle_test.go)
- CDN unreachable at runtime: proxy serves cached config; what happens to SSE; when clients see errors
- CDN unreachable at startup (cold start): four startup paths — cold, snapshot, snapshot_stale, empty_persistence (exit 1); which path triggers which behavior
- SSE upstream disconnect: reconnect loop behavior, poll interval fallback, client impact
- Snapshot write failure: async, never fails a request — what gets logged/metered
- Lifecycle events (tokenRotated, stageDeleted, projectDeleted): cache eviction + SSE teardown for the affected key
- Inactivity eviction: when keys are swept (idle > CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER, no active SSE subscribers), what gets cleaned up

**Health and readiness**
- /live vs /ready vs /health semantics and when each returns non-200
- What 'ready' actually means in terms of data availability

**Graceful shutdown**
- SIGTERM handling, drain timeout, exit codes

## Cross-references

After creating the doc:
- Add a link to docs/operations.md in README.md (Documentation section + a mention in 'How It Works')
- Add a 'See also: docs/operations.md' reference in: cache.md, sse.md, snapshot.md, monitoring.md, shutdown.md
- Add a doc-awareness comment header to each file in test/e2e/ so future LLMs reading those tests know docs/operations.md exists and should be updated when behavior changes. Format: a single-line comment at the top of each file, e.g.: // Behavior tested here is documented in docs/operations.md — update that doc when adding or changing tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- docs/operations.md exists and covers all sections above
- A reader can understand the full request and SSE lifecycle without reading any other doc
- Failure conditions match the behaviors asserted in test/e2e/outage_test.go, startup_test.go, and lifecycle_test.go
- README.md Documentation section links to docs/operations.md
- All five related docs/ files link to docs/operations.md
- All test/e2e/*.go files have the doc-awareness comment header

title: Improve README: replace ASCII art with Mermaid diagram and audit sections for accuracy
description:
The README is the entry point for anyone new to sdk-proxy. Two improvements needed:

1. **Mermaid diagram** — replace the ASCII art in 'How It Works' with a Mermaid sequence or flow diagram that clearly shows: SDK clients → proxy (cache hit / cache miss path) → CDN, and the SSE fan-out (N clients → 1 upstream connection). GitHub renders Mermaid natively in markdown.

2. **Section audit** — review each top-level section against the docs/ files to verify:
   - Content is accurate (e.g., the 5-minute revalidation note in 'How It Works' doesn't reflect the dynamic interval behavior added later — 10 min when SSE connected, 10 s when disconnected)
   - Content isn't duplicated verbatim by a docs/ file (README should summarize and link, not copy)
   - Nothing important is missing (e.g., OTel/tracing is mentioned only as a config variable, not in the architecture overview)

Acceptance criteria:
- ASCII art in 'How It Works' replaced with a valid Mermaid diagram that renders on GitHub
- Dynamic cache poll interval (10 min / 10 s) reflected accurately — not the stale '5 minutes'
- Each section either stands alone with accurate content or defers to the relevant docs/ file
- No section is a near-verbatim copy of a docs/ file

title: Remove raw SDK key from cache.Entry.FetchURL
description:
cache.Entry.FetchURL stores the full upstream CDN URL which contains the raw SDK key in the path. This is intentional (in-memory use is explicitly permitted by CLAUDE.md), but it is a latent leakage risk upheld by convention: any code that logs or serializes an Entry struct could inadvertently expose the raw key.

Fix options:
- Replace FetchURL with a structured type that separates the key-safe base URL from the SDK key component, reconstructing the full URL on demand.
- Or store only the SDK key hash and reconstruct the full URL at fetch time from CDN base domain + region + key.

This should be addressed when the cache Entry struct is next refactored, or when a structured public SDK key identifier is available to replace the hash.

title: fix(cache): deduplicate concurrent cold-miss upstream fetches with singleflight
description:
Two concurrent requests for the same uncached SDK key will both fan out to Cloudflare, since there is no in-flight deduplication in the cache miss path (proxy/handler.go ServeHTTP → serveMiss). Under low concurrency this is harmless, but at scale (many SDK instances cold-starting simultaneously) it produces N×M upstream requests where 1×M would do.

The fix is to wrap the upstream fetch in golang.org/x/sync/singleflight keyed on the cache key (SHA-256 hash). The first goroutine fires the request; concurrent goroutines for the same key block and share the result.

Acceptance criteria:
- Concurrent cold-miss requests for the same SDK key produce exactly one upstream HTTP call.
- The shared result is written to the cache and served to all waiting goroutines.
- Singleflight errors propagate correctly (all waiters get the error, not just the first).
- Existing unit and integration tests continue to pass.

Note: this is the singleflight fix referenced in the beads memory entry 'cache-stampede-on-cold-start-multiple-concurrent-requests'. After completing this issue, update that memory to reflect that the limitation has been resolved.

title: feat(cache): evict inactive cache entries to stop polling unused SDK keys
description:
The background refresher polls CDN for every SDK key in the cache, regardless of whether any SDK client has recently requested that key. When the proxy is long-running and SDK keys rotate or projects are deleted without sending lifecycle events, the cache can accumulate entries that are polled indefinitely even though no client will ever request them again.

The fix: track last-access time on each cache entry. A background sweeper evicts entries that have not been requested for longer than a configurable inactivity window (default: 2x SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE = 48h). Eviction also closes the upstream SSE connection for the affected key (same as the lifecycle event path).

## Design considerations
- Last-access time is updated on every cache hit (both served-from-cache and after a cold-miss warm path)
- The sweeper runs on a configurable interval (candidate: 1h) as a background goroutine
- Eviction is the same operation as lifecycle event invalidation (cache evict + SSE close)
- Entries evicted by inactivity are NOT written back to the snapshot store — the existing snapshot represents the last known state
- On next request after eviction, the entry is treated as a cold miss (fetches from CDN, populates cache)
- Configurable via CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER env var (default 48h); set to 0 to disable

## Acceptance criteria
- Cache entries not accessed for > CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER are evicted by the sweeper
- Eviction closes the upstream SSE connection for that key (reuses lifecycle eviction path)
- A subsequent request for an evicted key triggers a cold CDN fetch
- Metric proxy.cache.inactivity_evictions.total incremented per eviction
- Setting CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER=0 disables the sweeper entirely
- Existing snapshot state is preserved — eviction does not delete snapshot entries
close_reason: Implemented inactivity sweeper with full GC eviction, CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER config, HasSubscribers liveness gate, and proxy.cache.inactivity_evictions.total metric. All quality gates pass.

title: Add OTel metric for SSE streaming state transitions
description:
The DX reviewer flagged that operators have no OTel visibility into how many cache keys are in connected vs. disconnected SSE state, or when they transition. This makes it hard to verify that the dynamic-interval feature is working and that CDN load is actually being reduced as expected.

Add a gauge metric (e.g., proxy.sse.streaming_keys or proxy.sse.connections{state=streaming}) in internal/metrics/metrics.go. Record it in sse.Manager when the streaming state transitions via setStreaming — increment on true, decrement on false. Include sdk_key_hash label for per-key visibility.

This was deferred from sdk-proxy-ahq during code review phase 5.

title: Add pre-parse byte-length guard on lifecycle SSE event data
description:
Currently the cap in parseKeyHashes fires after json.Unmarshal has already allocated memory for the full payload. A malformed upstream can still cause a bounded ~1.6 MB allocation (10,000 × ~160 bytes) before rejection.

Add a byte-length check on evt.Data before Unmarshal — e.g. reject if len(evt.Data) > maxLifecycleEventBytes (configurable, default 1 MB). This closes the memory-amplification vector entirely and is complementary to the existing LIFECYCLE_KEYS_CAP guard.

Scope: internal/sse/lifecycle.go (parseKeyHashes), internal/config/config.go (new env var LIFECYCLE_EVENT_MAX_BYTES), docs/configuration.md.

title: test: add /health endpoint to e2e harness and smoke-test it
description:
The e2e test harness (test/e2e/harness.go) registers /live and /ready but not /health. The health package unit-tests /health, but a regression in the harness wiring or in health.Handlers.Health would not be caught by make test-int.

**Fix:**
1. Add mux.HandleFunc("/health", probeHandlers.Health) to the harness mux.
2. Add a test (in startup_test.go or helpers_test.go) asserting GET /health returns 200 when the proxy is ready.

**Why:** monitoring.md documents /health as a supported endpoint; e2e coverage should back that claim.

title: test: redact SDK key in billing_test.go error messages
description:
Two test error messages in test/e2e/billing_test.go leak raw SDK key values in CI/test output:

1. Line ~76: t.Errorf uses %q on TestSDKKey directly, printing the literal token.
2. Line ~124: t.Errorf uses %v on telemetry.Sample, which relies implicitly on Sample.String() redaction — fragile if String() changes.

**Fix:** Replace raw key references with cache.Key(TestSDKKey) and use explicit field access (s.KeyHash, s.Count) instead of %v on Sample.

**Why:** Keeps the SDK-key-never-in-logs invariant consistent in test output, and makes the redaction explicit rather than implicit.

title: test: assert SSE ConnCount==0 in lifecycle StageDeleted/ProjectDeleted tests
description:
TestLifecycle_StageDeleted_InvalidatesKey and TestLifecycle_ProjectDeleted_InvalidatesKey assert cache eviction but do not verify that the upstream SSE connection closes (ConnCount drops to 0). The test docstrings and monitoring.md both state that these events close the upstream SSE connection, so the test coverage is incomplete.

**Fix:** Add an eventually assertion checking h.SSE.ConnCount() == 0 at the end of both tests, matching the pattern already used in TestLifecycle_TokenRotated_InvalidatesKey.

**Why:** Ensures the SSE fan-out invariant (N clients → exactly 1 upstream connection) is validated after lifecycle invalidation for all three event types.

title: Add 404 log tracing for unrecognized proxy paths
description:
The catch-all 404 handler at / (added in sdk-proxy-jj5) uses bare http.NotFound with no structured log entry. Per observability requirements, dropped requests should leave a trace.

Options:
- Add a thin slog.Warn wrapper around http.NotFound, then file a follow-up to dedup/throttle (scanners will spam logs)
- Alternatively, instrument via OTel traces instead of log lines so high-volume paths don't flood the log stream

Choose the approach before implementing. The log spam risk is the main constraint.

title: docs: document always-exit-0 on SIGTERM policy
description: run() returns nil from the shutdown case (SIGTERM/SIGINT received), even when srv.Shutdown or the listener returns a non-nil error. This is intentional — on a signal-driven shutdown, errors are logged via slog.Warn and the process always exits 0. Process supervisors and CI pipelines that watch exit codes will not see a failure exit from a shutdown error. This policy should be documented in CLAUDE.md or a SIGTERM handling ADR so future contributors understand it is deliberate and do not inadvertently revert it.

title: feat(config): make billingShutdownGrace configurable
description: billingShutdownGrace is currently hardcoded to 10s in cmd/proxy/main.go. Operators running behind slow billing endpoints or with strict SLAs may need to tune this value. Add BILLING_SHUTDOWN_GRACE env var to internal/config (default 10s, validated > 0 and <= 60s at startup) and thread the value through to run(). The const in main.go can then be removed.

title: refactor(sdkkey): consolidate extractRegion / validateSDKKeyRegion into internal/sdkkey
description: Both internal/proxy/handler.go and internal/sse/handler.go contain a private copy of the same SDK key format validator (dt_server_{region}_{token}). The two copies will drift as the SDK key format evolves. Extract the canonical implementation into a new internal/sdkkey package and update both callers to import it. No behavior change expected.

title: feat(config): make SSE heartbeat interval configurable
description: The SSE keepalive heartbeat interval is currently hardcoded to 15s in cmd/proxy/main.go. Operators behind proxies or load balancers with aggressive idle timeouts may need a shorter interval. Add SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL env var (default 15s) to internal/config, validate it is > 0 and <= 60s at startup, and thread it through to sse.NewHandler.

title: research(config): evaluate OpAMP for dynamic remote configuration
description:
OpAMP (Open Agent Management Protocol) is an OTel ecosystem standard for remotely managing observability agents. Before committing to a purely static configuration model, we should understand whether OpAMP applies to sdk-proxy's use case — particularly for dynamic log level changes and feature toggles without service restarts.

What to investigate:
- What OpAMP provides: remote config push, health reporting, agent self-updates
- Fit evaluation: does sdk-proxy's role (a request proxy, not an OTel collector) match the OpAMP model?
- Go client library options (e.g. open-telemetry/opamp-go)
- Operational complexity: OpAMP requires a supervisor/management server — is that acceptable in our deployment model?

Deliverable: a brief write-up captured in the issue notes recommending adopt, defer, or reject with rationale. No code changes expected from this spike.

title: Add key_hash label to proxy.cache.inactivity_evictions.total
description:
The inactivity evictions counter currently has no labels, so all evictions accumulate into a single time series. This is intentional for now (evictions are rare fleet-level events and per-key cardinality would be high), but it means operators cannot tell which SDK keys are being evicted without cross-referencing logs.

Consider adding a key_hash label if per-key eviction visibility becomes operationally valuable. Evaluate cardinality impact before enabling in high-SDK-key-count deployments.

This was deferred from sdk-proxy-840 (inactivity eviction feature).

title: Add upper bound validation for CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER
description:
Currently there is no maximum value enforced for CACHE_INACTIVITY_EVICT_AFTER. A very large value (e.g. years) would compile and run but would mean the sweeper effectively never evicts, wasting memory and upstream SSE connections.

Add a maximum validation (suggested: 720h / 30 days) at startup. Values above the max should fail with a descriptive error pointing to the sensible range.

This was deferred from sdk-proxy-840 (inactivity eviction feature) as a low-priority polish item.

title: perf(telemetry): replace slice-shift eviction with ring buffer in BoundedRetryBuffer
description: The current BoundedRetryBuffer.Enqueue uses copy(b.buf, b.buf[1:]) to evict the oldest element when full. This is O(n) per eviction. Under sustained billing endpoint outages, every Enqueue on a full buffer copies the entire slice, causing measurable CPU spikes at large buffer sizes. Replace with a head-index ring buffer so both Enqueue and Drain are O(1). This was deferred from sdk-proxy-1hj during code review (Warning #3) as premature for MVP with default size 1000.

value: Cache stampede on cold start is RESOLVED. singleflight was added in sdk-proxy-566: concurrent cold-miss requests for the same SDK key now share one upstream call via singleflight.Group keyed on SHA-256(sdk_key). Side effects (cache.Set, SSE notification, snapshot write) fire exactly once per dedup batch. No further action needed for this limitation.
